howTo.title: How to Test
items: Tap the blue screen or press Space/Enter to start
When the red screen ("Wait") turns green ("NOW!"), press immediately. The signal appears at a random time between 1.5 and 5 seconds
Pressing before the signal or reacting in under 100ms counts as a false start and the round is repeated
After 5 rounds, see your average, median, percentile (reference) and tier, and share a result card to challenge friends

standards.title: Reaction Time Standards (approx., web + mouse)
items: 330ms and above: you may be tired or on a high-latency setup. Touchscreens normally score slower than these bands

whatIs.title: What is the Reaction Time Test?
whatIs.description: It measures your simple visual reaction time in milliseconds: press as fast as possible the moment the screen changes color. Simple visual reaction time measured in labs is typically 200–250ms; web tests add mouse and display latency, so around 250–280ms is common. You get the average, median and best of 5 rounds, and records are saved in this browser so you can track your trend.

tips.title: Tips
items: Look at the center of the screen and keep your finger resting on the button while you wait.
One slow round now and then is normal. The median reflects your skill better than the average.
Fatigue, lack of sleep and alcohol noticeably slow reaction time. Testing at the same time of day shows how your condition changes.
A wired mouse and a high refresh-rate display (120Hz+) reduce equipment latency.

items.q: What is an average reaction time?
items.a: Simple visual reaction time in lab settings is typically 200–250ms. Web tests add input and display latency, so around 250–280ms is common; under 200ms is quite fast.

items.q: Are touch-screen results accurate on mobile?
items.a: Touchscreens add input-detection and display latency, so results are usually tens of milliseconds slower than a wired desktop mouse. Compare records on the same device.

It is generally accepted that a visual signal takes at least about 100ms to travel through the brain to the finger muscles. Faster inputs are treated as anticipation (guessing the timing) rather than reaction, so the round is repeated.

items.q: Is reaction speed directly tied to gaming skill?
items.a: Reaction speed is only one factor; game sense, prediction and aim accuracy matter too. In fast-paced games like FPS, though, a lower reaction time is an advantage.
